headline: Middle East disruption and softer NAM drag results lower
summary_short: Weatherford's Q2 2026 revenue fell 8.2% y/y to $1,105M as all three segments (DRE, WCC, PRI) declined on Iran-conflict-driven Middle East disruption and softer North America activity, with operating income down 54.9% y/y to $107M and diluted EPS falling to $0.55 from $1.87.
summary_long: Revenue fell 8% y/y and 4% q/q to $1,105M as all segments declined — DRE, WCC and PRI — on Iran-conflict Middle East disruption and softer North America activity, partly offset by growth in Europe/Sub-Sahara Africa/Russia. Gross profit fell 11% y/y to $333M as costs decreased slower than revenue. Operating income dropped 55% y/y to $107M, hurt by the revenue decline and the absence of a prior-year $70M Argentina divestiture gain. Net income fell 71% y/y to $39M; diluted EPS fell to $0.55 from $1.87. Cash rose to $1,100M from $943M a year ago. No quantitative guidance was issued; management reiterated its 3-5%-of-revenue capex framework for 2026.

drivers.explanation: All three segments declined as Iran-conflict-related disruption hit Middle East/North Africa/Asia activity and North America softened, partly offset by growth in Europe/Sub-Sahara Africa/Russia; the prior year also included a $70M gain on the Argentina pressure-pumping sale that did not repeat.

Q2 revenue decline was led by DRE (44% of the drop) and WCC (23%), with PRI and lower integrated-services/projects activity making up the rest; MENA fell $78M and North America $36M, partly offset by a $13M Europe/Sub-Sahara Africa/Russia gain.
Cost of products and services fell 7% y/y on lower product sales and reduced headcount, but slower than revenue's decline, pushing the cost ratio to 70% from 69% and compressing gross profit.

Decline was primarily due to lower revenue and the non-repeat of the prior-year $70M Argentina pressure-pumping sale gain, partly offset by lower cost of products/services, restructuring and R&D spend.

Tracks the operating-income decline and a higher D&A run-rate ($71M vs $64M a year ago); the 10-Q does not itself define an 'EBITDA' line — this figure is Yahoo's fundamentals-timeseries derivation, distinct from management's own non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA of $223M disclosed in the Q2 2026 earnings release.

Fell in step with the revenue and operating-income declines; partly cushioned by lower income tax expense ($33M vs $46M) on decreased pre-tax earnings and a lower interest expense following 2025 debt refinancing.
Declined in step with net income on a roughly flat diluted share count (~72.2M shares in both the current and prior quarter).
